findings.element: Exhibit 3 — 2026 consensus table, 'KEY VIEW' column
findings.detail: The 'Key View' column text is visibly cut off for every institution row (e.g., Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, BCA Research, IBRC/Stanford). The cell content is truncated with no ellipsis or tooltip, making the commentary unreadable in a board context.

findings.element: Sector tiles — commentary bullet text beneath GDP figures
findings.detail: The small-print commentary lines beneath each sector tile (Passenger Airlines, Hotels, Restaurants, etc.) are rendered at an extremely small font size — estimated 6–7 px — making them illegible at normal viewing distance or when printed in a board deck.

findings.element: Exhibit 4 — Six 2026 themes, body paragraph text
findings.detail: The five numbered theme paragraphs at the bottom of the page are rendered at a very small font size (estimated 7–8 px). At board-deck print resolution this text would be unreadable.

findings.element: Exhibit 3 — 2026 consensus table, 'RANGE / SCENARIO' and 'FED RATE PATH' columns
findings.detail: Several cells in the 'Range / Scenario' and 'Fed Rate Path' columns appear to have text clipped at the cell boundary without wrapping, causing partial loss of content for multiple institution rows.

findings.element: Exhibit 1 'So what' commentary
findings.detail: The 'So what' note reads as a single compound sentence rather than the 2–4 sentence structure required. It does not clearly separate the signal from the implication, reducing executive clarity.

findings.element: Sector tiles grid — 'Federal Government' and 'Freight & Logistics' bottom row
findings.detail: The bottom row of sector tiles contains only two tiles, leaving a large blank area to the right. This creates a visibly unbalanced grid compared to the three-column rows above it, which would appear unfinished in a board presentation.

findings.element: Vertical gap between Exhibit 3 (consensus table) and the sector tiles section
findings.detail: The vertical whitespace between the consensus forecast table and the sector GDP tiles block is noticeably larger than the spacing between other exhibit sections on the same tab, creating an inconsistent rhythm.

findings.element: Sector-level mini bar charts — year labels and growth rate figures
findings.detail: The annual data labels (e.g., '2021', '2022', '2023', '2024') and the small percentage figures inside each sector panel are rendered at a font size that is extremely difficult to read at normal viewing distance. A board-level audience would struggle to extract the underlying numbers without zooming in.

findings.element: Per-sector commentary text (e.g., 'State/Local Govt', 'Residential RE', 'Federal Govt', etc.)
findings.detail: The one-to-two line commentary beneath each sector mini-chart is rendered at a very small font size (appears to be ~7–8 px equivalent), making it effectively unreadable without zooming. This is below the minimum body-copy size required for CEO-level presentation materials.

findings.element: Bottom data-source footnote
findings.detail: The multi-line sources footnote at the very bottom of the tab is rendered in extremely small, low-contrast grey text. While footnotes are expected to be small, the current size makes it completely illegible even at full resolution.

findings.element: Filter bar labels ('Consumer & Leisure', 'Food & Grocery', 'Travel & Transport', etc.)
findings.detail: The category filter pill labels are rendered at a very small size and low contrast against the pill background, making them difficult to read quickly in a board presentation context.

findings.element: GDP Commentary block — right edge
findings.detail: The GDP Commentary paragraph text appears to be cut off at the right edge of the commentary box ('…multiplier effects on consumption, residential investment, and business capex. Downside risk to sub-1% growth in the next two quarters is material and rising.'). It is unclear whether the full sentence is visible or whether the container is clipping the final words.

findings.element: Sector grid — bottom two rows (Cruise Lines, Travel Agencies)
findings.detail: The final row contains only two sector panels (Cruise Lines and Travel Agencies) while all other rows contain five panels, leaving a large blank area to the right. This creates a visually unbalanced grid that looks unfinished in a board deck.

findings.element: Summary table ('Real GDP held 2.0% in 2025') vs. sector grid above
findings.detail: The vertical gap between the bottom of the sector mini-chart grid and the top of the summary table section appears noticeably larger than the inter-panel gaps within the sector grid, creating an inconsistent rhythm on the page.

findings.element: Federal Govt sector commentary
findings.detail: The Federal Govt panel commentary appears to contain a hedging qualifier ('…as we are sometimes not included in payrolls'). Per style guide, commentary must be direct and free of hedging filler language.

findings.element: Exhibit 4 — Sector Wage Growth Bar Chart y-axis sector labels

findings.detail: The source and methodology footnote beneath Exhibit 3 is rendered in very small, low-contrast gray text that is effectively illegible at normal viewing scale.

findings.element: Exhibit 5 — Sector Wage Table source footnote block

findings.element: Exhibit 4 — Sector Bar Chart, several y-axis sector labels

findings.element: Wage Growth Commentary — fc-note text block at top of tab
findings.detail: The commentary block contains hedging language ('essentially zero', 'look resilient') and runs to what appears to be 3–4 dense sentences that border on exceeding the conciseness standard. findings.element: Exhibit 3 — Real Wages Annual Bar/Line Chart
findings.detail: Exhibit 3 plots two series (Nominal and Real/inflation-adjusted) but the legend, if present, is extremely small and difficult to confirm as visible. At board-deck scale it is not clearly legible, risking the audience being unable to distinguish the two series.

findings.element: Gap between Exhibit 2 and the Exhibit 3/4 row
findings.detail: There is a noticeably larger vertical gap between the Exhibit 2 full-width chart panel and the two-column Exhibit 3/4 row below it compared to the spacing between other panel rows on the same tab, creating visual inconsistency.

findings.element: KPI tile — 'Stickiest Category'

findings.element: Exhibit 5 — Annual CPI bar chart, x-axis year labels

findings.element: Exhibit 5 — Annual CPI bar chart, bar value labels

findings.detail: The 'So what' commentary reads: 'Rates need to break below ~5.5% to unlock the lock-in cohort — until then, transaction volume stays compressed and price discovery is thin.' This is a single sentence, falling below the minimum of 2 sentences required by the style guide.

findings.element: EX 3 'So what' callout text
findings.detail: The 'So what' commentary ('Affordability deterioration has compounded — the price-to-income gap is the structural drag on transaction volume.') appears to be a single sentence, below the 2-sentence minimum.

findings.detail: The 'So what' commentary ('Fed cuts don't automatically translate to mortgage relief — the long-end + MBS spread is the binding constraint, not the policy rate.') appears to be a single sentence, below the 2-sentence minimum.

findings.detail: The full-width source citation row at the very bottom of the page is rendered in extremely small text, making it effectively illegible. While footnotes are often small, this text appears to fall below any reasonable minimum threshold.
